top_issues.issue: Fuel/hull bars are flat, thin, saturated rectangles with tiny labels
top_issues.why: Every other emissive in the brief blooms softly into the dark. These bars look like default progress bars and are the least on-tone element in the HUD, even though they are the most important resources
top_issues.suggested_direction: Thicken them slightly, add a faint inner glow or soft bloom in the bar colour, darken the empty track, and push the labels and values up a size for legibility

top_issues.issue: Title UI sits over a lit, busy tile field instead of darkness
top_issues.why: Reference 01 is about a dark shaft with warm light rising from far below. Here the wordmark competes with a bright, gridded orange ground, which weakens both the mood of descent and the contrast behind the small text
top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken or vignette the area behind the title stack, toward black in the middle and warm glow near the bottom, so the wordmark and button float over void

top_issues.issue: The ending body copy is long italic text at low contrast
top_issues.why: Six centred italic lines in grey are tiring to read and dilute the strong OUT moment
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use upright text at a slightly higher value, add more line spacing or split it into beats, and consider a subtle prompt or mark to fill the lower third

top_issues.issue: Small secondary labels (LUMENS, CARGO, layer name, title footer key hints) are very small and faint
top_issues.why: Readability of play comes first. At 1280x800 these labels are near the edge of legibility
top_issues.suggested_direction: Raise the secondary label size and value by one step, and keep the letterspacing

top_issues.issue: Glow is a square tile-clipped halo rather than bloom that lands on the rock
top_issues.why: Each emissive fills its own cube face with a flat radial wash that stops hard at the tile edge. Neighbouring stone isn't lit, which breaks the 'light lands' principle and reads as tinted tiles.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the glow spill past the tile onto adjacent faces as a soft falloff (point light or a shared bloom pass), and tighten the in-tile halo so it concentrates near the ore base.

top_issues.issue: Iron vanishes against host rock
top_issues.why: Non-glowing iron needs value and specular contrast. The dark gunmetal faces sit at the same value as the dark rock, so the ore is lost at gameplay size.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lift iron's lit faces to a cooler, brighter gunmetal-blue with a hard specular rim and a few brighter blue glints, keeping it non-emissive.

top_issues.issue: Pale ores collapse into one look at gameplay size
top_issues.why: Silver, diamond, frostbloom and nacre all use a pale grey-lavender halo and spiky white geometry, so the brief's distinctness pairs blur at 50px.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop or minimise the halo on silver (specular only), give diamond a cool ice-blue tint and sparkle points, and give nacre a ribbed fan silhouette with a pink-teal sheen instead of points.

top_issues.issue: Silver needles detach from the base
top_issues.why: Blades float apart from the nub, and one variant is a scatter of loose slivers, so it reads as broken geometry rather than a fan erupting from rock.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Root all needles at a common rock base and fan them upward; make them slightly thicker so they survive at 50px.

top_issues.issue: Gold and nacre silhouettes drift from the concept
top_issues.why: Gold is a yellow lump with rock caps, not rock with a golden wound. Nacre is a crystal rosette, not a scalloped shell.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Gold: mostly matte rock boulder with a broad cracked opening glowing amber. Nacre: layered, ribbed fan or shell on slate with a soft sheen rather than a hard glow.
